title: Quest-backed link, rename and unlink fail after mutating documentation and task state
summary: Quest-backed link, rename and unlink fail after mutating documentation and task state
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

In a fresh disposable Git repository with the installed pair:
  quest init --name repro --task-id-prefix R
  lore init --yes --tracker quest
  quest task create "Repro task" --id R-1 --actor repro-agent --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human fixture-owner --json
  lore new story "Repro story" --summary "Coupling reproduction" --json
  lore link stories/repro-story R-1 --json
Observed: exit 6, reporting that tracker quest supplied repository file .quest/tasks/R-1.json and non-backlog trackers do not own paths in this repository. Both the Story and Quest task have already changed. Repeating the link also fails. Rename/unlink exercise the same persistence boundary.
Source lead: src/adapters/quest.ts maps value.file ?? value.path to the detail file; src/tracker-persistence.ts rejects a non-null file for Quest. src/commands/link.ts records/validates this after the tracker edit. Investigate this boundary rather than making Quest pretend its records have no location.
Impact: normal coupling reports failure after authoritative writes; retry does not establish a trustworthy success receipt. Orbitfall needed explicit Quest --doc/--label references followed by lore link --no-back-ref, then inspection of both sides. That workaround does not resolve ordinary coupling.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An installed Lore/Quest pair links, relinks, renames and unlinks with consistent references on both sides and no unintended Git commit.
Invalid persistence data is rejected before mutation, or partial application is explicitly reported with recovery instructions.
Regression tests compare before/after bytes of both the Story and Quest record for success, failure and retry.
